name: auth-broker
description: Identity broker for the multi-SSO sign-in: GitHub (device flow + web), Google (web code flow + PKCE) and Cloudflare One (Access JWT), owner only (#1066, #1083)

auth_broker._doc: THE allowlist: the only identities the broker admits. Google: `allowed_emails` (verified email, exact match). GitHub: `allowed_github` (login AND numeric account id must both match; `email` is the identity handed to the gate). No email-domain rule exists on purpose (a domain-wide rule would admit every address at that domain). Sign-in: GitHub uses the OAuth device flow (RFC 8628: the broker shows a user code and the provider's verification link, polls the provider); Google uses the standard web authorization-code flow with PKCE S256 and a single-use state bound to the browser (callback paths below). Either way the provider's user is then checked against these lists. Each provider has its own `enabled` flag; a disabled provider refuses new sign-ins but its instance still validates the shared session cookie. The guard src/test in infra-sec_caddy (test-multi-sso.sh) fails when these lists hold anyone else, or a domain-wide rule appears; infra-sec_auth-broker/src/test/test-broker.py exercises the device flow against stub providers.

providers.label: Google
providers._doc_flow: Web application client (sops: AUTH_BROKER_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID/SECRET). Redirect URIs registered at Google must equal redirect_uris exactly. The consent screen is in Testing mode: the owner account must be a listed test user.

providers.label: GitHub
providers._doc_client_id: The GitHub CLI's public OAuth client id (device flow, no secret). Public by design; not a credential.

web._doc: The owner's own GitHub OAuth App (web redirect flow, PKCE + state). client_id is public. The client secret is sops key AUTH_BROKER_GITHUB_APP_CLIENT_SECRET: until it is present the web leg stays off and /oauth2/github/start serves the device flow (gh public client above, also reachable with ?flow=device). GitHub allows one callback URL per App: auth. only.

providers.label: Cloudflare One
providers._doc_flow: Cloudflare One (Zero Trust) sign-in. <prefix>/start (on the chooser hosts in `hosts`) sends the browser to `login_url`, a hostname that Cloudflare Access protects (cloud-infra c_vps/ba-clo_cloudflare terraform.json zero_trust.broker_app: Access app + owner-only policy, proxied through the fleet tunnel straight to this instance). After the Access login, Cloudflare forwards the request with Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion; <prefix>/callback verifies it (RS256 against the team certs, issuer, audience in cloudflare_access.aud, expiry, owner email only), issues the shared _diego_sso cookie and 302s to rd (an https URL under rd_domain; a relative rd is resolved against the chooser host it came from). A request without a valid JWT gets 401 and no cookie. No client id or secret exists for this provider.

cloudflare_access._doc: Cloudflare Access (Zero Trust) as a fourth credential: the broker verifies Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion (RS256 signature against the team certs, issuer, audience, expiry) and admits only a token whose email is in allowed_emails (service-token JWTs carry no email and are refused). `aud` lists the AUD tags of the Access applications trusted (terraform outputs zt_pilot_aud and zt_broker_aud in cloud-infra c_vps/ba-clo_cloudflare; zt_broker_aud is the Cloudflare One sign-in app, #1083). Served on every instance at <prefix>/cf-auth; the edge gate calls it when the request carries the header.
